commit.message:
fix: a project pursuit whose release fails says so, keeps its Theorem and starts no other (#17)

ProjectPursuit ignored Coordinator.release()'s answer: Stop reported
released on RELEASE_FAILED, and a spent Coordinator's failed release let
the next Theorem start while the first still held nodes. A release that
fails now leaves the pursuit release-failed, its Theorem current, with
the reason; Stop answers RELEASE_FAILED and may be tried again, and once
a retry gives the runs back the pursuit is released. Nothing starts
meanwhile: the loop ends, and Start is refused (PURSUIT_ACTIVE). A
Coordinator that ended release-failed on its own holds the pursuit too.

Closes #17

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: a pursuit is stopping until its release returns, and waits for one already under way (#17)

PR #23 review (fddd978): a retried Stop said released before its release
returned, so a new Start pursued T2 while T1 still held its node; and a
COORDINATOR_ACTIVE answer, another Stop releasing the Coordinator, was
taken for nothing to release, so the budget path started T2 at once.
Stop now holds the pursuit stopping, refusing Start, until the release
ends released or release-failed; a second Stop meanwhile returns the view.
_release waits for a release under way and asks again: NO_COORDINATOR once
it gave the runs back, this one's own try once it failed. Any other
refusal is a failed release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: the #17 budget-path tests end T1's run instead of leaving it running (#17, #18)

#18 (PR #24) has the Coordinator wait, at its budget's end, for the runs
still going. These two tests spent the budget with T1's run still going
and would wait forever under it; ending the run, keeping its claim, is
the same path under either behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -865,6 +865,79 @@ def test_a_spent_coordinator_whose_release_fails_holds_the_next_theorem_until_st
     assert worlds["T2"].runs["T2"].starts == 0
 
 
+def _gated(run):
+    """The run's release held until `finish` is set; `entered` once it is under way."""
+    import threading
+
+    entered, finish, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event(), run.release
+
+    def held(*args, **kwargs):
+        entered.set()
+        assert finish.wait(5), "the release gate timed out"
+        return release(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    run.release = held
+    return entered, finish
+
+
+def test_a_stop_retried_after_a_failed_release_is_stopping_until_it_returns_and_no_start_begins_meanwhile():
+    """PR #23 review: the retry said `released` before its release returned, and a new Start pursued T2 while T1 held its node."""
+    import threading
+
+    worlds = {"T1": World(edges={"T1": []}, kinds={"T1": "claim"}), "T2": World(edges={"T2": []}, kinds={"T2": "claim"})}
+    pursuit, _ = _pursuit(worlds)
+    pursuit.start("claude")
+    _until(lambda: worlds["T1"].runs["T1"].starts == 1, "T1 pursued")
+    worlds["T1"].runs["T1"].fail_release = True
+    assert pursuit.stop()["code"] == "RELEASE_FAILED"
+    _until(lambda: not pursuit.active(), "the pursuit's thread ended")
+    worlds["T1"].runs["T1"].fail_release = False
+    entered, finish = _gated(worlds["T1"].runs["T1"])
+    retried = []
+    stopper = threading.Thread(target=lambda: retried.append(pursuit.stop()), daemon=True)
+    stopper.start()
+    assert entered.wait(5)
+    view = pursuit.view()
+    assert (view["status"], view["current"]) == ("stopping", "T1")
+    assert pursuit.start("claude")["code"] == "PURSUIT_ACTIVE" and "error" not in pursuit.stop()   # a second Stop waits on the first
+    time.sleep(0.05)
+    assert worlds["T2"].runs["T2"].starts == 0
+    finish.set()
+    stopper.join(5)
+    assert "error" not in retried[0] and retried[0]["status"] == "released" and worlds["T1"].runs["T1"].status == "released"
+
+
+def test_a_spent_coordinator_already_being_released_by_another_stop_holds_the_next_theorem_until_that_release_ends():
+    """PR #23 review: COORDINATOR_ACTIVE (another Stop releasing it) was read as nothing to release, and T2 started at once."""
+    import threading
+
+    worlds = {"T1": World(edges={"T1": []}, kinds={"T1": "claim"}, budget=(1, 60.0)), "T2": World(edges={"T2": []}, kinds={"T2": "claim"})}
+    pursuit, made = _pursuit(worlds)
+    coordinator, run = made["T1"], worlds["T1"].runs["T1"]
+    entered, finish = _gated(run)
+    release, answers = coordinator.release, []
+
+    def overlapped():   # the researcher's Stop on T1's Coordinator lands just before the pursuit's own release
+        if not answers:
+            threading.Thread(target=release, daemon=True).start()
+            assert entered.wait(5)
+        answers.append(release())
+        return answers[-1]
+
+    coordinator.release = overlapped
+    pursuit.start("claude")
+    _until(lambda: run.starts == 1, "T1 pursued")
+    run.end("budget", turns=1, reason="out of turns")   # the Coordinator's budget spent; the run ended, keeping its claim
+    _until(lambda: answers, "the pursuit's release asked")
+    assert answers[0]["code"] == "COORDINATOR_ACTIVE"
+    time.sleep(0.1)
+    assert worlds["T2"].runs["T2"].starts == 0 and pursuit.view()["current"] == "T1"
+    finish.set()
+    _until(lambda: worlds["T2"].runs["T2"].starts == 1, "T2 pursued once T1's runs were given back")
+    assert run.status == "released" and answers[-1]["code"] == "NO_COORDINATOR"
+    pursuit.stop()
+
+
 def test_stop_on_a_finished_pursuit_leaves_its_ending_as_it_was():
     worlds = {"T1": World(edges={"T1": []}, kinds={"T1": "claim"})}
     pursuit, _ = _pursuit(worlds)
